paragraphs: The GLA200 has been part of the GLA-Class range since the model launched in 2013, and across its two generations has used several different petrol engines — from the early M270 and M282 through to today's M260 and M282 units. Early cars (X156 generation, 2013–2020) used the M270 2.0-litre turbo petrol in pre-facelift form, with some later X156 models switching to the M282 1.3-litre unit. From 2020, the current H247 generation uses the M260 2.0-litre and continues with the M282 1.3-litre in some markets. The full breakdown by engine code is below.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every GLA200 on the road.

cards.body: A 2.0-litre turbocharged petrol four-cylinder fitted to the GLA200 from 2013 to approximately 2017 on the X156 generation. It's part of the same M270 family used across the Mercedes compact range of that era.

A 1.3-litre turbocharged petrol four-cylinder fitted to later X156 GLA200s (roughly 2017–2020) and continuing into the H247 generation from 2020. This is the smaller-capacity unit in the GLA200 range.
A 2.0-litre turbocharged petrol four-cylinder fitted to the current H247-generation GLA200 from 2020 onwards. It's part of the newer M260 family that replaced the M270 in many Mercedes applications.

compatibility.intro: Because the GLA200 spans multiple engine codes across its two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming parts from one engine will work on another — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic GLA-Class quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
